data.name: Pragun
data.gender_notes: Pragun is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who asks questions, one who inquires, one who seeks knowledge and wisdom. The name Pragun carries the meaning “Ask, Enquire, Question” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Pragun usually hope their child will grow to embody ask, enquire, question and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Encourages self-inquiry and introspection, fosters curiosity and intellectual growth
data.etymology: Pragun belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ask, Enquire, Question.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pragun total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Pragun holds great significance in Hindu culture as it reflects the importance of questioning and seeking knowledge in the Hindu tradition. In Hindu philosophy, the process of asking questions and seeking answers is considered a vital aspect of spiritual growth and self-realization.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Pragun also holds profound spiritual significance, as it echoes the central tenet of Hinduism: the pursuit of knowledge and truth to achieve self-realization and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Pragun: One who seeks truth with unwavering curiosity and wisdom. The name symbolizes the relentless pursuit of knowledge and the inner light that illuminates the path towards self-realization.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu scripture Mahabharata mentions a sage named Pragunaswami who was a disciple of Bhagiratha. He was a great sage who performed severe penance to please Lord Shiva and attain moksha.

Another reference to Pragun is in the Puranic text, the Vayu Purana, where it is mentioned that Pragunaswami was a sage who had the unique ability to see the past, present, and future. He was a revered figure among the sages and was known for his immense wisdom and spiritual insight.
